What do you cook with (and why should I use it?)

The following is based on my own experience.

You would do well to own more than 1 stove. 1 isobutane stove (snow peak giga power) and a liguid fuel stove ( msr whisperlite of any variety). The reason for this no 1 stove can do it all, it can come close but purpose built just does its job better. I bet if you ask any backpacker or backcountry enthusiast who has been around the mountain for awhile they will probably have a small stove collection.

I have used a snow peak giga power TI stove. I love it, bought it to replace my msr pocket rocket. I used this stove for three season. When the temp drops below 20 degs F. the fuel doesnt vaporize so well. This is when i opted for my msr simmerlite and i have used this stove down to -20 degs F. Recently i have gotten into home made prepackaged dehdrated meals so about 6 months ago i picked up the msr windboiler which fantastic for its role. Better than or worse than jetboil, i dont know but i do trust the msr name more than jetboil.

I have a few cooksets as well. Msr titan kettle. Snow peak TI trek 1400 and 3 sizes of the msr stowaway stainless steel pots. A 10 oz stainless steel gsi cup that fits on the bottome of nalgene liter bottle. Like the stoves the cooksets serve their niche very well. For the rough routes or car camping i really like the stowaway pots. For the times when i want to cook up a semi gourmet meal deep in the sticks for 1 to 3 people i will run the snow peak 1400. The titan kettle or stainless steal cup is an always present piece. The length, the degree of roughness and abusiveness of the trek determines which one i take along. My msr windboiler has really taken its place as a secondary, auxillary or support stove that is always in the day pack. I us it during overnight spike camping and quick hot water during pre dawn preping it also works great for dehydrated meals.

If i was cornered with only 1 pot and 1 stove to take i would go with a liguid fuel stove like the whisperlite universal and a 1 liter stainless steel pot with lid. My reason here is the weight is offset by the versitility and inherent ruggedness. An added plus is Stainles steel pots can be set on open flame or hot coals without worries just dont dry boil EVER! And stay away from non stick coating, it has no business on high demand cooking materials.

Remember, after learning the limitations of your system you will only be able to use it better and plan with it instead of around it.
